262 MB zip of comma-delimited text (three files per year, a, b and c). State government records (Type Code 0) exist only for FY1972 and FY1977-FY2012; the User Guide says liquor store data "appear to be missing from source files before fiscal year 1977, except" in census of governments years. The 2005 classification redesign left the liquor store items unchanged (2006 Classification Manual, Appendix 1.6.2).

Only the liquor store items of state governments are read: revenue (Census code A90) and expenditure (total, current operations E90, capital outlay F90 + G90), in thousands of current dollars. Census defines liquor stores as "alcoholic beverage distribution facilities operated by governments maintaining alcoholic beverage monopoly systems", so a wholesale-only monopoly (Mississippi, Wyoming, Michigan after its stores closed) has liquor store revenue too: a value never says that the state runs retail stores, and a zero never says it does not. Revenue "excludes any taxes collected by the system" (Glossary of Government Finances, 1992, in the IndFin zip); expenditure includes the purchase of liquor for resale. Census publishes no profit or transfer item, and the IndFin readme warns that a difference between revenue and expenditure "does not necessarily indicate a budget surplus or deficit", so none is computed here. Local government liquor stores (municipal and county ABC stores) are not read. The state-by-type files carry no layout document of their own; each line is read as Census state code, type digit (2 = state government), item code, amount in thousands, coefficient of variation and year, because on that reading every state government liquor item for FY2008-FY2012 equals the IndFin record (checked 2026-10-08, and kept as the validation check reconcile_census_liquor_store_files). The Technical Documentation in the FY2015-FY2024 unit zips documents the same layout (level code 2 = "State government total"); from FY2017 its state codes are FIPS codes, not Census codes.

The keyless v1 API returns at most 10 years per request, so the series is requested in four fixed windows. Setting BLS_API_KEY sends the same request to the v2 endpoint. The download.bls.gov bulk files refused this project's automated client (HTTP 403) on 2026-10-06. Responses carry a per-request 'responseTime' field, removed before hashing (normalize: bls_api_json) so the pin identifies the data.

Only SAPCE3 line 28, "Alcoholic beverages purchased for off-premises consumption" (millions of current dollars, 1997-2025), is read: spending by residents of each state on alcohol bought to take away from any store type (grocery, liquor, convenience and state stores alike). Drinks bought in bars and restaurants are in "food services" and are not separated. BEA's footnotes: (L) less than $50,000; (NM) not meaningful; the U.S. line differs from the sum of states by net expenditures abroad.

An experimental Census product. The file gives only the percent change from the same month a year earlier, by state, for total retail sales excluding nonstore retailers (code TOTAL) and for eleven three-digit NAICS subsectors; it holds no dollar levels, so nothing can be expressed per resident. Food and beverage stores (NAICS 445) mix supermarkets with beer, wine and liquor stores; no liquor-store detail is published. Values are not seasonally adjusted and not adjusted for trading days, holidays or prices (Census notes). The Census maps flag changes whose 90 percent confidence interval includes zero; this file carries no such flags, so the dashboard cannot show them. The exact download URL was not recorded.

Only NAICS 445310 (beer, wine and liquor stores) is read, for each state as a whole and the United States: establishments, sales (receipts) and paid employees. These are private businesses with payroll; the establishment counts match County Business Patterns (Pennsylvania 1,869 against 1,868 in 2017, Virginia 483 against 485), which excludes government-operated stores, so state-run liquor stores appear not to be counted. Receipts are all sales of these stores (they may include sales to bars and restaurants), not total alcohol sales in the state: grocery, convenience and drug stores, restaurants and state stores sell alcohol outside this measure. A "D" flag means withheld to avoid disclosing a single company; the file prints 0 in those cells, which is stored as missing (suppressed), never zero. The 2022 Economic Census "First Look" files in the same download hold national totals only and were superseded by the 2024 Geographic Area Statistics release (their read_me says so); they are not imported. The exact download URLs were not recorded.
